name: One-Unit Holonomy Anomalies Form a Trichotomy
statement: For a two-arm holonomy cycle with excess $\varepsilon=1$, exactly one configuration occurs: two disjoint two-concept shores with one uncounted lower-fiber vertex; two two-concept shores meeting in their common non-root owner; or disjoint shores of orders two and three. No additional nonempty passive coordinate occurs at cost one. If $\varepsilon=2$ and there are three nonempty passive coordinates, the third shore is a singleton disjoint from the two disjoint two-concept cycle shores, and the uncounted remainder is zero.
proof: In the exact two-arm budget, all terms are nonnegative integers. At excess one, an extra coordinate would itself cost one and every concept in its shore would add another exponential-incidence charge, so exactly the two cycle coordinates occur. The only remaining unit can be the uncounted remainder, one shared incidence of the two shores, or one additional shore member, giving the three cases. Gate holonomy shows that a shared concept cannot be either root, hence is the common owner. At excess two with a third coordinate, its coordinate charge and one concept charge exhaust the budget; overlap with a cycle shore would cost more, forcing the stated singleton profile.
